title: OpenAI tool-name normalizer and runtime shim for legacy function compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Customers are increasingly using OpenAI-style "tool" declarations and models that expect name-based routing and structured responses. Redwood's legacy function surface and our internal tool-signature model use different naming conventions, parameter encodings, and error/streaming semantics. This ticket implements a runtime shim that normalizes incoming OpenAI-style tool calls to Redwood's legacy function interface and vice versa for responses. Goals: - Provide deterministic name resolution rules (case, punctuation, aliasing) so model-specified tool names reliably map to the correct Redwood function. - Translate argument payloads (JSON schema / string-encoded args) to the expected legacy function signature. - Preserve streaming semantics: support streaming tool invocation bits + continuation behavior when functions return partial outputs. - Emit deprecation/compat telemetry when ambiguous names are detected and surface guidance for customers. Non-goal: full language-based prompt rewriting or model-side fixes. This is an engineering-first compatibility layer to reduce migration friction.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Name mapping deterministic: unit tests cover casing, punctuation, whitespace, underscore/dash aliases and a prioritized resolution order.
2) Signature mapping: adapter converts OpenAI-style JSON args to legacy arg lists and vice versa with schema validation and clear errors.
3) Streaming preserved: e2e tests show model-initiated streaming tool outputs flow through shim and are observed by SDK clients.
4) Rollout toggle: feature flag exists (RUNTIME_ENABLE_OAI_TOOL_SHIM) and can be toggled without reload.
5) Docs + migration: engineering docs and migration guide produced; two sample migrations (ImageAnnotator and BillingLookup).
6) Telemetry: emit name-ambiguous, mapping-failure, and shim-enabled metrics (counts and sample traces).
tasks: RFC: design name-resolution precedence and alias rules (owner: Marcelo)
Implement name-normalizer module (unicode normalization, strip punctuation, canonical tokenization)
Signature translator: arg marshaling and validation harness (supports JSON schema and legacy tuple args)
Runtime shim: integrate into request routing path and function-invoker interface
Streaming passthrough tests: harness model->shim->function->client with partial-chunking
Feature flag + rollout script + config docs
Docs: migration guide + examples + SDK behavior notes
Add telemetry hooks and sampling for ambiguous resolves
Security review (if needed) and perf benchmark run
notes: Design decisions: 1) Namespaces: prefer exact full-name match; then canonicalized match (lower+punct stripped); then aliases defined in function registry; then warning + 409 with suggested candidate if ambiguous. 2) Error semantics: mapping failures surface structured error with mapping_hint field to aid automated retries. 3) Backwards compat: legacy function callers are untouched unless feature flag enabled. 4) Performance: canonicalization is CPU-light and cached per-function name; benchmark target is <150us median cost per resolve.
